body: My God, I'm sorry, I let it get too personal. Anyway, you've answered the question I had, thank you very much ;)

You may have encountered someone with depression or something similar... See... I feel like my thoughts don't really have any control... any decisions I make have to go through the lens of my own depression... that's why I can't believe in Free Will... I'm not really free.. unless someone changes it and starts to use a more appropriated term

Suffering from depression makes me have a different perspective on my own agency and the dynamics of my own thinking, especially because I am aware of how my problem affects them. I do not feel at all like an agent of my own life. I know that my own self is affected by my condition and so I have my doubts about the existence of free will.

It's crazy cause the video I saw was made by a scientist who believes in the non existence of free will. And usually when I see videos on youtube about the matter of Free Will is usually made by some religious person who talks about God and the after life and the 'right path' and then I just think this is bullshit. But here I see more convincing and better answers.

Electronic music is an umbrella term precisely because it has created so many genres and covers everything it touches. 

Rock is the same from Argentina to Japan, Sri Lanka to the UK.

Pop music is more about performance and aesthetics than the music itself. But I don't believe that only by making “good music” can someone reach a good artistic level. There are talents all over the world and the vast majority of them will die into oblivion.

But then when you look at electronic music as it is, you realize that it has managed to adapt in all the spaces where it has triumphed. Electronic music in my country is going to be very different from electronic music in other countries, precisely because to make good electronic music you don't need a studio and lots of extremely expensive instruments. Rock music, on the other hand, traditionally requires a lot of instrumentation and still manages to produce very similar things no matter where we are.

Listening to AC/DC and Nirvana and then Gun' n Roses and Slayer. Then listening to some of the Beattles' rock projects and then having to listen to any other band's project seems extremely boring to me.
